headline: PUN reports noise-aware planning results on geometric 2D–4D benchmarks
summary: A new preprint introduces Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that maps obstacle geometry, goal, cost and noise inputs to a desirability field, then uses bounded local search to guide stochastic replanning. On the authors’ 4D geometric benchmark it reports 95–100% success at 10.51–11.66 ms/start across four tested noise levels. The paper says compared methods share the saved test queries and noise sequence, but PUN timings use a B200 GPU while listed baseline timings use faster CPU implementations; only one trained model per dimension is evaluated. The method assumes control–noise matching, and the authors report no full robot/contact models and continued difficulty on adversarial mazes. These are credible but unconfirmed paper-reported results, not a demonstrated robotics deployment.
